title: Duchy of Głogów
capsule: The Duchy of Głogów was a Silesian Piast duchy created from the fragmentation of the Duchy of Silesia, with Głogów (German: Glogau) on the Oder as its capital. During the attested window (1250–1314) it was ruled by the Piast line descending from Conrad I of Głogów; Conrad II (died 1273) and then Henry III (died 1309) consolidated the territory before it passed to Henry's five sons, who divided it further into appanage fragments. The duchy's strategic location on the middle Oder made it contested between the Piast princes and the expanding Bohemian Crown under the Přemyslid and later Luxembourg dynasties. By 1331 Bohemian suzerainty over Głogów was established, and the duchy was absorbed into the Bohemian Crown lands.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The duchy's core territory around Głogów is identified through Piast dynastic records and Bohemian administrative sources, but boundaries of the various sub-divisions created by partitions among Piast heirs are only approximately reconstructed.
